review_messages:
Independent read-only review of MUSIC_CRAFT_RELEASE_20261013/worker, compared directly against the previously reviewed FILM_CRAFT_RUNTIME_RELEASE_20261013 producer/publisher pair and published HANDOFF.md.

BASELINE PINS ARE REAL (not invented): build_id quiz-2026.10.13-film-craft-adf95a5, source_commit adf95a57594158308c94ee2bff1cb5ca9c9c0684, archive_sha256 5ed5fdf6...654c85, image sha256:6d2a206a...75daa6, counts 132/4048/248 all match HANDOFF.md's published Helm49 figures verbatim. Target math (132+1=133 packs, 4048+4=4052 questions, 248+4=252 articles, 9+1=10 runtime cache) is internally consistent.

VERDICT: this is a shape-validator stub, not a useful concrete producer, and does NOT meet the assignment's explicit bar ('must become runnable by the authorized lead once those concrete prerequisites exist'). Four concrete issues:

1) prepare_music_craft_release.py's main() calls validate(load(manifest)) and then UNCONDITIONALLY calls fail('intentionally not prepared...') regardless of whether validate() succeeded. I manually constructed a fully well-formed manifest (correct baseline dict, correct target dict, all contract strings, valid-format commit/hashes, correct status) and confirmed it still raises every time -- there is no input, however genuine, that lets this script ever stage anything. That is 'do not implement execution', not 'do not execute in this worker': Film Craft's prepare_film_craft_release.py, by contrast, actually extracts the prior archive, copies/verifies real frozen git blobs by hash, appends the runtime cache, writes checksums, and builds a verified tar.gz when given correct inputs (status PREPARED_NOT_EXECUTED) -- it only defers the remote SSH/Helm/kubectl cutover to a separately gated publisher. Music Craft's version defers/disables staging itself, which is a materially smaller and non-conforming deliverable.

2) require_hash() only checks SHA256 regex format, never compares against any real file or git blob -- package_sha256/main_dart_js_sha256/catalog_sha256/reader_sha256/review_evidence_sha256 are accepted as long as they look like hex, with zero content verification. Film Craft's equivalent (sha256_file, git_bytes + hash checks against FROZEN_FILM_FILES/FROZEN_CATALOG_SHA256/etc.) verifies real bytes. Music Craft has no such mechanism at all, so 'hash' fields are currently decorative.

3) publish_prepared.py is a 2-branch stub: --preview or --publish immediately raise RuntimeError, nothing else. None of the README's required future gates (fresh backup, tested rollback, image pin, old-source preservation, copied-DB grading/history, public verification, no-ETag-conditional) exist as implemented logic anywhere, even inert/unreachable. Film Craft's publisher, by contrast, has a fully worked prepare()/publish_script() that performs real local validation and script assembly and is gated behind an explicit, currently-unused --publish branch with an explanatory comment that it isn't invoked by this task. Music Craft's publisher has no equivalent implementation to gate.

4) negative_checks.py only exercises 'manifest file missing' and 'one fully-valid manifest' (which only reaches the always-on final fail). It does not test any of validate()'s ~9 individual rejection branches (wrong baseline dict, stale Helm48 build_id, altered target counts, placeholder status, mismatched contract strings, incomplete review, invalid commit format). I independently ran six manual tamper cases (altered target count, placeholder status, stale Helm48 baseline, incomplete review, bad hash format, fully valid) directly against prepare_music_craft_release.py myself and confirmed each currently raises the correct distinct error -- so the validate() logic itself is sound today -- but the repository's own test suite does not prove this and would not catch a regression in any single branch. This is exactly the kind of self-test gap the task asked me to flag: PASS here does not constitute coverage of the stated rejection behaviors.

BOUNDED CONCRETE REWORK (does not require guessing any future commit/image/hash): (a) remove the unconditional fail() in main() and implement real staging mirroring Film Craft's pattern -- read/verify real frozen content via git blobs and real sha256_file checks once a genuinely frozen manifest supplies real paths/commit, then extract/copy/append-cache/write-checksums/archive, keeping the remote/irreversible cutover itself gated to a separate, explicitly-authorized publisher (same split Film Craft already uses); (b) make the five *_sha256 manifest fields verified against real bytes, not just hex-shape; (c) implement publish_prepared.py's required gates (backup/rollback/image pin/preservation/copied-DB/public-verification/no-ETag-conditional) as real, --publish-gated logic analogous to the Film Craft publisher, even if --publish itself stays unused by this worker; (d) add negative_checks.py cases for each individual validate() rejection branch (one tampered field at a time) so the suite actually proves the rejection logic instead of only proving two aggregate outcomes.

Recommend REWORK.
